stem: Let $n_1(x)=\frac{x^2-{=a2}}{x-{=a}}$ and $n_2(x)=x+{=a}$. Both reduce to $x+{=a}$. Mark on the number line the value of $x$ that is excluded from the common domain, so the two functions are not equal there.
solution: The denominator $x-{=a}$ is zero when $x={=a}$, so $x={=a}$ is outside the domain of $n_1$.
$n_2(x)=x+{=a}$ is defined for every real number, so the common domain is $\mathbb{R}-\{{=a}\}$.
Mark $x={=a}$: the simplest forms agree, but the domains differ, so $n_1\neq n_2$.
notes: Lesson 3-2 has no anchor book question; parent is the nearest anchor in the lesson (bk-drill-1-4). Empty or incomplete marking means the student compared only the simplest forms. sign-flipped (marking -a, reading x-a=0 as x=-a) and extra-values have no misconception in this objective's list, so they are left unmapped. Targets use the instance field a as a number in the list.
